outcome.technical: Reviewed the prep diff: drive-phase.open_findings now delegates to audit-task open_findings via _loader.load_script; of1-of3 added in test_drive_phase, of1 in test_audit_task. Open point answered: YES the drive got stuck - pending findings carried no fixTask and answer_refusal accepted --answer fix for any open id, but audit-task _fixes_targets refuses 'already names X as its fix task' for a finding naming a task, so a finding whose fix closed --no-change was offered fix and add_fix_tasks stopped. Fixed: the pending finding dict now carries fixTask (keys list in the triage builder) and answer_refusal only counts findings with no fixTask as fixable, so such a finding reads 'not open' for fix and is left to --answer sign-off, which records --accept-open (disposition). Added of4 (fix over a fixTask finding refused) and of5 (fix over a free finding not refused); reflowed the STAGES line. Results: test_drive_phase 138/138, test_audit_task 926/926, ruff clean. test__deps FAILS 306/307, case r2: new edge governance/drive-phase.py runtime-loads audit-task (layer 8) from layer 8, not strictly downward. The structural fix is to move SETTLED_STATUS + open_findings into scripts/manifest/_manifest_phases.py (lower layer; audit-task and drive-phase both read it). I tried; require-plan REFUSED the edit to _manifest_phases.py (not in this task's files; declared by done tasks only, subagent may not widen scope), so I reverted my two dependent edits and the tree is back to the loader version. Orchestrator must either widen P122.11-z4y files to include _manifest_phases.py (then the move is mechanical: define the two names there, alias them in audit-task.py, call _phases.open_findings in drive-phase.py, drop the loader line) or add a KNOWN_LAYER_DEBT entry in _deps.py.
